context: 3 Open problems This paper naturally leads to some questions. Can we restrict ourselves to points moving polynomially in order to find a kinetic net? More precisely: I Problem 1. Let d ≥ 2, β be integers and r ≥ 1. Is there a pair c(d, β, r), g(d, β) such that for any finite set P of points moving polynomially with bounded description complexity β in Rd there exists a kinetic weak 1r -net for P of cardinality at most c(d, β, r) and description complexity g(d, β) whose points move polynomially? Let d ≥ 1, β be fixed integers and c(d, β, r) be as in theorem 4. We didn’t prove any lower bound on c(d, β, r), so the current best lower bounds coincide with those in the static case which are Ω(r logd−1 r), see [3]. This leads to the following research direction.
